en: An indeterminate, non-conditioning state is not a condition, by way of object condition, for an indeterminate, non-conditioning state.
An indeterminate, non-conditioning state is a condition, by way of object condition, for a wholesome, non-conditioning state.
An indeterminate, non-conditioning state is a condition, by way of object condition, for an unwholesome, non-conditioning state.

Condition: An indeterminate (abyākata) state that is not a condition is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for an unwholesome (akusala) state that is not a condition and for an indeterminate state that is not a condition.
An indeterminate state that is not a condition is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome (kusala) state that is not a condition and for an unwholesome state that is not a condition.
Five with respect to object; five with respect to predominance and decisive support. (The unconditioned is similar to that which has no condition.)
